trap-negation-contrast.evidence: 1 negation-contrast construction(s): ", not locally." — state the positive claim directly

Eight instances, four of them the SAME contrast restated in the opening paragraph alone: (1) 'Phi_n acts globally, not locally.' (2) 'It is not built per-vortex and combined by tensor product.' (3) 'Instead Phi_n forms the global section...' (4) '...determined by its compatibility with the Frobenius-Hopf substrate axioms..., not by an additive combination of local pieces.' Then: (5) 'evaluates globally to zero ..., not locally trivialised by some spectator structure'; (6) 'The conjecture is no longer "find the local NF generators and combine". It becomes "find the categorical global section..."'; (7) 'Demanding that Phi_n form a single global section, rather than a colimit of local pieces'; (8) 'as a structural prediction rather than a numerical phenomenon'.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: The global-vs-local distinction IS the block's claim, so any ONE of these would be the documented substantive-contrast false positive. Fourfold restatement of one contrast in a single opening paragraph is not. PROPOSED (not applied -- consolidating four sentences into one is a rewrite beyond the 2-sentence inline budget): keep sentence (3) as the positive statement, delete (2) and the trailing clause of (4), reduce (1) to 'Phi_n acts globally.'

trap-superlative.evidence: '**The only consistent reconciliation** requires global topological neutrality at saturation' and 'It provides the structural reason a non-trivial action **cannot** coexist with finite mass at saturated n' -- two unqualified maximum-strength claims (a uniqueness claim and a scope-(b) structural exclusion) in a block whose own final paragraph states 'It makes no new logical claim.' The supporting argument is two informal 'flaws', neither proved: flaw 1 asserts 'the accumulated flux at the descent limit diverges' with no bound and no citation; flaw 2 is 'finite observable mass'.
trap-superlative.notes: PROPOSED (not applied -- these are scope claims, meaning at stake): 'The only consistent reconciliation requires' -> 'The reconciliation proposed here is'; 'a non-trivial action cannot coexist with finite mass' -> 'a non-trivial action is not expected to coexist with finite mass'. AGENTS.md STRICT: a scope-(b) exclusion ('cannot appear in any closure') requires a CITED proved invariant -- parity/sign, a dimension or degree bound, a Lean-proved impossibility. None is cited; the argument is a divergence heuristic, which is scope (a).
